h: Four Rescues Reveal How Shabbos Repairs Every Fallen Soul

p: What the Baal Shem Tov instituted,
to say the psalm "Give thanks to Hashem" (Tehillim 107),
the four who must give thanks,
the holiness radiates from the root,
and all the blemishes and corruptions are rectified
"Whom He redeemed from the hand of the oppressor,
and gathered them from the lands"
that is, from every kind of earthiness
from the four corners of the earth,
"from the east and from the west,
from the north and from the sea";
כְּעִנְיַן אָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א)
like what they said, of blessed memory (Berachos 17a):
and the subjugation to the kingdoms"
for through the leaven in the dough
that is in the souls of Yisrael,
of the aspect of the yetzer hara
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ שְׁלִיטָה עֲלֵיהֶם
through this there is dominion over them
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב)
And as it says in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 2):
it is as if all of you were exiled."
And when the time of rectification comes,
all the sparks of holiness are gathered
from the four corners of the earth.
And after this are mentioned in detail
all kinds of descents and falls
that are found in each individual soul
throughout the days of the week;
and for all of them there is a rectification
from the radiance of the root,

p: this alludes to a person who goes about idle,
that has been neither sown nor worked.
And this is "in a desolate way":
"Fortunate are those whose way is perfect,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem."
as they said, of blessed memory (Kiddushin 40b):
nor in Mishnah nor in proper conduct
is not part of civilized society";
for he does not find the "settled city,"
and he is called a boor, like a wilderness.
and the Tree of Life is Torah.
but to hear the words of Hashem."
that is, he is so coarsened
by the matters of this world
"For the ways of Hashem are straight";
that he be of the aspect of civilization.
"Let them thank Hashem for His kindness,
for He satisfied the longing soul,
and filled the hungry soul with good";

p: "Those who dwell in darkness and the shadow of death" (Tehillim 107:10):
this alludes even to those who transgress to provoke,
"For they rebelled against the words of God
and spurned the counsel of the Most High";
Therefore they are called "those who dwell in darkness,"
and they are "bound in affliction and iron,"
for they are, in this world,
and has no way to get out
there is a rectification for this too
and then "He brings them out of darkness and the shadow of death," etc.
And that is: "Fools, because of their sinful way,
and because of their iniquities, are afflicted"
that is, the aspect of desire and anger;
the beginning of the first sin
was in the desire for eating,
and from it came the other desires,
through this the soul becomes loathsome.
And through crying out to Hashem,
which is the words of Torah
and rescues them from their pits of destruction";
הַיְינוּ מִבְּחִינַת שְׁנֵי הַפְּגָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל
that is, from the aspect of the two blemishes mentioned above,
which is known to be like avodah zarah,
and as it says in the Gemara (Shabbos 105b)
"There shall be no strange god within you"
"Which strange god is within one's body?

p: "Those who go down to the sea," etc. (Tehillim 107:23);
this alludes to one who is harried by his thoughts
to remove the turmoil of his thoughts,
as they said, of blessed memory (Yevamos 121a):
עַל כָּל גַּל וָגַל שֶׁעָבַר עָלַי וְכוּלֵּי
"At each and every wave that passed over me," etc.
for he has no peace of mind;
"and they cried out to Hashem," etc.,
are included all kinds of descents and falls
and through the radiance of the holiness of Shabbos
And this is: "He turns a wilderness into a pool of water,
and a parched land into springs of water," etc.;
"Whoever is wise, let him keep these things in mind":
is waiting and hoping for this,
"And his father kept the matter in mind,"
"He kept watch for me at the doorway,"
and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
That is, one must be wise
even though he does not yet feel
עִם כָּל זֶה יְיַחֵל אֶל ה׳
nevertheless he should hope to Hashem,
be strong and let your heart take courage,
"And they will understand the kindnesses of Hashem":
the kindnesses of Hashem upon him.

p: when he was created on the sixth day,
there was immediately, in the first corruption,
מֵעֵין כָּל הַד׳ פְּגָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל
something of all four blemishes mentioned above;
as they said, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 38b):
was a denier of the fundamental principle,"
וְגַם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יט)
and they also said, of blessed memory (Bereishis Rabbah, parsha 19),
that he said, "I ate and I will eat more,"
וְגַם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יט, ט)
and they also said, of blessed memory (Bereishis Rabbah 19:9):
and now according to the will of the serpent";
that is, the serpent troubled his thoughts
of the addition of the holiness of Shabbos,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good"
before the entrance of Shabbos Kodesh into the world:
for all of man's deeds to be rectified,
as at the beginning of Creation.
For the creation of the sixth day
וּבָזֶה יוּבַן מַאֲמַר חֲזַ״ל (שַׁבָּת קנו, א)
And with this the statement of Chazal will be understood (Shabbos 156a):
One who is born on the sixth day
will be a man who pursues mitzvos;
and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
"For such is the way of Erev Shabbos,
to go after the mitzvos of Shabbos."
like the traits of all the other weekdays,
as with the first day of the week:
"a man without one thing in him,"
which is like the beginning of Creation
whereas they were not then exerting themselves
However, from the very beginning of Creation
the creation of man on the sixth day,
that man be occupied with mitzvos;
"And He placed him in Gan Eden
to work it and to guard it";
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן נה)
and they said, of blessed memory (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55):
"'To work it' — this is the positive mitzvos;
'and to guard it' — this is the negative mitzvos."
the day of Erev Shabbos is sanctified
for man's preparation from his side,
"And it shall be on the sixth day
that they shall prepare what they bring in."
And one may say this is the allusion
as in "A person should always set
שֻׁלְחָנוֹ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵּי (שַׁבָּת קיט, ב)
his table on Erev Shabbos," etc. (Shabbos 119b);
the essence of the holiness of the Shabbos night meal
is the preparation of the arousal of holiness,
to draw it upon himself from man's side.
And it is called by the name
which alludes to the souls of Yisrael,
which comes from the side of arousal from below;
and therefore it is called "Erev Shabbos,"
כְּעִנְיַן אָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג, א)
like what they said, of blessed memory (Avodah Zarah 3a):
כִּי הַשֵּׁם הָעֶצֶם שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
was given to the arousal of the soul from its own side.
And the holiness of the day of Shabbos
and therefore it is called "Atika Kaddisha,"
which is the flow of the root
